issues.detail: Error handling is thin: only one UBT compile error is covered, and it omits common failures such as missing Visual Studio or SDK components, a stale Live Coding build, failed cooks, and Linux-only commands with no Windows or macOS equivalents shown.

scenarios.name: blueprint-friendly-enhanced-input-character
scenarios.rationale: B satisfies every rubric item, with EditAnywhere MaxHealth, a BlueprintNativeEvent OnDeath with an _Implementation body, Enhanced Input BindAction with ETriggerEvent, the mapping context added through the subsystem, and a damage function named ApplyHit; A meets the input and death-event items but overrides TakeDamage, which the rubric explicitly forbids.

scenarios.name: fix-undeclared-enhanced-input-build-error
scenarios.rationale: Both add the EnhancedInput module dependency, the include, and the .uproject plugin entry, but A gives a complete Build.sh command with the project path and an explicit project-file regeneration step, while B regenerates files only generically and its Build.sh command is correct but less thorough, though it does include -project.

scenarios.name: package-shipping-build-linux
scenarios.rationale: Both use RunUAT.sh BuildCookRun with the correct project, platform and clientconfig, and both include -archivedirectory; B states plainly to run from the engine root and lists the exact -build -cook -stage -pak -archive flags, while A calls RunUAT.sh through $UE_ROOT without saying to run from the engine root and adds extra flags (-allmaps, -compressed, -package) beyond the rubric.
